summary: First checkpoint of the blueprint for global Galois duality and compact coefficients, within RS-08's boundaries. It plans R02.1: lim and lim¹ of towers with the six-term sequence and the Mittag-Leffler vanishing, the Milnor sequence for towers of complexes, continuous cochains into inverse limits and their lifting along finite surjections, the comparison with Mathlib's continuousCohomology carrier, Tate's inverse-limit theorem, continuous sections and long exact sequences, rationalisation, the discrete quotient V/T and the torsion of H¹(T), and the pointwise-Hom/splitting-torsor interface of Harpaz–Wittenberg's Lemma 5.5 in corrected form. The other stages are not yet read.

nodes.title: lim and lim¹ of a tower
nodes.statement: For an ℕ-indexed tower of abelian groups (A_n, φ_n : A_{n+1} → A_n), lim A = ker(∏A_n → ∏A_n) and lim¹A = coker(∏A_n → ∏A_n) for the shift (a_n) ↦ (a_n − φ_n(a_{n+1})). These compute R⁰lim and R¹lim, and R^p lim = 0 for p > 1.
hypotheses: ℕ-indexed towers only; for other index sets the derived functors are different.
proofSteps: Definition as kernel and cokernel of the shift map.
Identification with Rlim is Stacks Lemma 15.88.1.
acceptance: lim¹ is kept explicitly in every comparison until a Mittag-Leffler lemma removes it (RS-08).

sources.locator: Stacks Project, More on Algebra, Lemma 15.88.1 (tag 07KW)
sources.excerpt: The functor lim : Ab(N) → Ab has a right derived functor Rlim ... for any (An) in Ab(N) we have R^p lim An = 0 for p > 1, the object Rlim An of D(Ab) is represented by the complex ∏An → ∏An, (xn) ↦ (xn − f_{n+1}(x_{n+1})) sitting in degrees 0 and 1, if (An) is ML, then R^1 lim An = 0

nodes.title: Mittag-Leffler towers
nodes.statement: A tower is Mittag-Leffler if for every n the images of A_{n+k} → A_n stabilise as k grows.
hypotheses: Stated on the underlying sets, as in the Stacks Project; for groups the images are subgroups.
proofSteps: Definition through the iterated transition maps.
acceptance: Mathlib's CategoryTheory.Functor.IsMittagLeffler is the same notion for functors to types; the tower form is the one the lim¹ lemmas consume.

sources.locator: Stacks Project, Algebra, Definition 10.86.1 (tag 0594)
sources.excerpt: Let (Ai, φji) be a directed inverse system of sets over I. Then we say (Ai, φji) is Mittag-Leffler if for each i ∈ I, the family φji(Aj) ⊂ Ai for j ≥ i stabilizes.

nodes.title: Mittag-Leffler towers have vanishing lim¹
nodes.statement: If (A_n) is Mittag-Leffler then lim¹ A = 0.
proofSteps: Replace A_n by the stable images, which form a tower with surjective transitions and the same lim¹; for surjective transitions, solve a_n − φ_n(a_{n+1}) = b_n by induction on n (Stacks Lemma 15.88.1).
acceptance: The converse fails for uncountable systems; for towers of countable groups it holds (not needed here).

nodes.title: The six-term sequence of lim and lim¹
nodes.statement: For a short exact sequence of towers 0 → A → B → C → 0 there is an exact sequence 0 → lim A → lim B → lim C → lim¹A → lim¹B → lim¹C → 0.
hypotheses: Exactness levelwise; compatibility with the transition maps.
proofSteps: Snake lemma for the map of short exact sequences 0 → ∏A → ∏B → ∏C → 0 given by the shift maps.
acceptance: With A Mittag-Leffler, 0 → lim A → lim B → lim C → 0 is exact (Stacks Lemma 10.86.4).

sources.locator: Stacks Project, Algebra, Lemma 10.86.4 (tag 0598)
sources.excerpt: Let 0 → Ai → Bi → Ci → 0 be an exact sequence of directed inverse systems of abelian groups over I. Suppose I is countable. If (Ai) is Mittag-Leffler, then 0 → lim Ai → lim Bi → lim Ci → 0 is exact.

nodes.title: The Milnor sequence for towers of complexes
nodes.statement: For a tower of cochain complexes of abelian groups (K_n) with degreewise surjective transitions and limit K = lim K_n, there are short exact sequences 0 → lim¹ H^{p−1}(K_n) → H^p(K) → lim H^p(K_n) → 0.
hypotheses: Degreewise surjective transitions, so lim K_n computes Rlim K_n.
proofSteps: 0 → K → ∏K_n → ∏K_n → 0 (shift) is a short exact sequence of complexes (surjectivity of the shift from degreewise surjective transitions).
Its long exact cohomology sequence has connecting maps whose kernels and cokernels are lim and lim¹ of H^•(K_n).
acceptance: The lim¹ term is kept; it vanishes under Mittag-Leffler (mittag-leffler-lim-one).

sources.locator: Stacks Project, More on Algebra, Lemma 15.88.10 (tag 07KY), with Lemma 15.88.9 (tag 07KX)
sources.excerpt: the long exact cohomology sequence associated to the distinguished triangle breaks up into short exact sequences 0 → R^1 lim_n H^{p−1}(K_n) → H^p(Rlim K) → lim_n H^p(K_n) → 0

nodes.title: Lifting continuous cochains along finite surjections
nodes.statement: For a compact totally disconnected space X (for example Gⁱ with G profinite) and a surjection π : Y → Z of finite discrete sets, every continuous f : X → Z lifts to a continuous g : X → Y. Hence for a tower of finite discrete G-modules with surjective transitions, the transitions C^i(G, T_{n+1}) → C^i(G, T_n) are surjective.
hypotheses: X compact and totally disconnected; Y, Z discrete, π surjective.
proofSteps: f is locally constant with finitely many fibres, each clopen; compose with a set-theoretic section of π.
acceptance: Fails for connected X mapping to a non-trivial finite set only in the trivial way; the profinite hypothesis is what makes cochain towers Milnor-admissible.

sources.locator: Appendix B, §2, Proposition 2.3, printed p. 152 (PDF p. 162)
sources.excerpt: Proposition 2.3 ([T4] Corollary 2.2, [J] §2). Suppose i > 0 and T = lim← Tn where each Tn is a finite (discrete) G-module. If H^{i−1}(G, Tn) is finite for every n then Hi(G, T) = lim←n Hi(G, Tn).
sources.match: Tate's inverse-limit statement relies on this surjectivity.

nodes.title: Continuous cochains into an inverse limit
nodes.statement: For G profinite and T = lim T_n (inverse-limit topology), C^i(G, T) = lim C^i(G, T_n) as complexes, and the transitions of this tower are surjective when the T_n are finite discrete with surjective transitions.
hypotheses: T closed in ∏T_n with the product topology.
proofSteps: Continuous maps into a subspace of a product are compatible families of continuous maps into the factors (continuous_pi_iff).
Surjectivity from cochain-lifting.
acceptance: The coboundaries commute with the limit because they are given by the same formula levelwise.

nodes.title: Comparison with the canonical carrier for compact coefficients
nodes.statement: For a profinite G and a topological G-module T whose underlying module is compact (a lattice T, a finite discrete module) or a finite-dimensional ℚ_p-space, Mathlib's continuousCohomology (homogeneous cochains on the coinduced resolution) is naturally isomorphic to the cohomology of the inhomogeneous continuous cochain complex C^•(G, T).
hypotheses: The comparison for discrete T is Tau Ceti ProfiniteCohomology Layer 3; this node extends it to compact and rational coefficients.
proofSteps: The dehomogenisation map between homogeneous and inhomogeneous continuous cochains is a homeomorphism Gⁱ⁺¹ → Gⁱ-shape bijection, continuous in both directions for any topological module, so the discrete proof applies verbatim once continuity is checked on the compact-open topology.
acceptance: Every later statement is on the canonical carrier, as RS-08 requires.

nodes.title: Tate's inverse-limit theorem
nodes.statement: For G profinite, T = lim T_n with finite discrete G-modules T_n and surjective transitions, and i > 0, there is a short exact sequence 0 → lim¹ H^{i−1}(G, T_n) → H^i(G, T) → lim H^i(G, T_n) → 0. In particular H^i(G, T) = lim H^i(G, T_n) when every H^{i−1}(G, T_n) is finite.
hypotheses: i > 0; finite discrete T_n; surjective transitions.
proofSteps: cochains-inverse-limit: C^•(G, T) = lim C^•(G, T_n) with surjective transitions.
milnor-sequence gives the short exact sequence.
Finite H^{i−1}(G, T_n) form a Mittag-Leffler tower (Tower.isMittagLeffler_of_finite), so lim¹ = 0.
acceptance: Applied with T = ℤ_p(1), i = 1: SelmerIwasawaCohomology's p-adic Kummer identification.

sources.locator: Appendix B, §2, Proposition 2.3, printed p. 152 (PDF p. 162)

nodes.title: Continuous sections of coefficient surjections
nodes.statement: A surjection T → T'' of topological G-modules has a continuous set-theoretic section when T'' is discrete, when T' is open in T, or when T is a finitely generated ℤ_p-module or a finite-dimensional ℚ_p-vector space with its natural topology.
hypotheses: The listed cases, as in Rubin Remark B.2.2.
proofSteps: Discrete T'': any set-theoretic section is continuous.

Finitely generated ℤ_p-modules and finite-dimensional ℚ_p-spaces: the surjection splits ℤ_p- (resp. ℚ_p-) linearly up to a finite torsion part, which is handled by the profinite case (continuous sections of surjections of profinite groups).
acceptance: The section need not be a homomorphism.

sources.locator: Appendix B, §2, Remark 2.2, printed p. 152 (PDF p. 162)
sources.excerpt: Note that if T′′ is topologically discrete ... then there is always a continuous section T′′ → T. This is the case whenever T′ is open in T. Also, when T is a finitely generated Zp-module, or a finite-dimensional Qp-vector space, with the usual topology, there is a continuous section.

nodes.title: Long exact sequences for continuous cohomology
nodes.statement: If 0 → T' → T → T'' → 0 is exact and has a continuous set-theoretic section T'' → T, then 0 → C^•(G, T') → C^•(G, T) → C^•(G, T'') → 0 is exact and there is a long exact sequence in continuous cohomology, natural in the sequence, agreeing with Tau Ceti's discrete one when all terms are discrete.
proofSteps: Surjectivity of C^i(G, T) → C^i(G, T'') by composing with the section; the rest is the long exact sequence of a short exact sequence of complexes.
acceptance: Without a section the cochain sequence need not be right exact.

nodes.title: Continuous cochains into V land in a lattice
nodes.statement: For a compact space X, a finite free ℤ_p-module T and V = T ⊗ ℚ_p, every continuous f : X → V lands in p^{−n}T for some n; hence C(X, V) = ⋃_n C(X, p^{−n}T) = C(X, T) ⊗ ℚ_p.
proofSteps: f(X) is compact, hence bounded in the p-adic norm.

sources.locator: Appendix B, §2, Proposition 2.4, printed p. 152 (PDF p. 162)
sources.excerpt: Proposition 2.4 ([T4] Proposition 2.3). If T is a finitely-generated Zp-module, then for every i ≥ 0, Hi(G, T) has no divisible elements and the natural map Hi(G, T) ⊗ Qp → Hi(G, T ⊗ Qp) is an isomorphism.

nodes.title: Rationalisation of lattice cohomology
nodes.statement: For G profinite and T a finitely generated ℤ_p-module with continuous action, H^i(G, T) has no nonzero divisible elements and H^i(G, T) ⊗ ℚ_p ≅ H^i(G, T ⊗ ℚ_p).
hypotheses: T finitely generated over ℤ_p with the p-adic topology.
proofSteps: compact-cochain-bounded: C^•(G, V) = C^•(G, T) ⊗ ℚ_p, and ⊗ ℚ_p is exact.
Divisible elements: they map to 0 in every H^i(G, T/p^n) and so lie in the lim¹ term of tate-inverse-limit, which Tate shows has no divisible elements.
acceptance: V's cohomology is not the limit of anything; rationalisation is a colimit.

sources.locator: Appendix B, §2, Proposition 2.4, printed p. 152 (PDF p. 162)
sources.excerpt: Proposition 2.4 ([T4] Proposition 2.3). If T is a finitely-generated Zp-module, then for every i ≥ 0, Hi(G, T) has no divisible elements and the natural map Hi(G, T) ⊗ Qp → Hi(G, T ⊗ Qp) is an isomorphism.

nodes.title: Cohomology of the discrete quotient W = V/T
nodes.statement: For T finite free over ℤ_p, W = V/T is a discrete torsion module and H^i(G, W) = colim_n H^i(G, W[p^n]), with W[p^n] ≅ T/p^nT.
hypotheses: G profinite; W with the discrete topology (a continuous action on V/T makes it a discrete module).
proofSteps: A continuous cochain Gⁱ → W has compact, hence finite, image, contained in some W[p^n]; cohomology commutes with this filtered colimit (Tau Ceti ProfiniteCohomology, finite-quotient description, Layer 4).
acceptance: T and W have different topologies and different limiting operations, as the stage requires.

nodes.title: The sequence T → V → W and the torsion of H¹(T)
nodes.statement: For T finite free over ℤ_p, the sequence 0 → T → V → W → 0 gives V^G → W^G → H^1(G, T)_tors → 0, and ker(H^1(G, T) → H^1(G, V)) = H^1(G, T)_tors.
proofSteps: continuous-section-long-exact applies because W is discrete.
rationalization identifies ker(H^1(T) → H^1(V)) with the torsion subgroup.
acceptance: H^1(G, T) is torsion-free when W^G is divisible (for example W^G = 0).

nodes.title: Pointwise Hom of discrete modules
nodes.statement: For discrete Γ-modules C and A, Hom_pt(C, A) is the group of additive maps C → A with the topology induced from A^C (pointwise convergence) and the conjugation action (g·u)(c) = g u(g⁻¹c). Evaluation Hom_pt(C, A) × C → A is jointly continuous and equivariant, and the action is jointly continuous. For finitely generated C the topology is discrete, and Hom_pt(C, A) is Tau Ceti's InternalHom with homAction.
hypotheses: C, A discrete; no finiteness on C for the definition.
proofSteps: Induced topology from the product; continuity of evaluation from continuity of projections; discreteness for finitely generated C: evaluation at finitely many generators isolates 0.
acceptance: No derived-functor (Ext) interpretation is claimed for Hom_pt with non-discrete topology.

nodes.title: The splitting torsor
nodes.statement: For an exact sequence 0 → A → B → C → 0 of discrete Γ-modules admitting an additive section, the sections form a continuous affine Hom_pt(C, A)-torsor under conjugation; a section s gives the continuous cocycle γ(g) = g s g⁻¹ − s with values in Hom_pt(C, A); replacing s by s + u changes γ by d⁰u; the class [γ] vanishes iff there is an equivariant additive section.
hypotheses: An additive section exists; Hom_pt with the pointwise topology (not the discrete one).
proofSteps: Two sections differ by a map C → A; conjugation preserves sections; the cocycle identity is formal; continuity of γ into Hom_pt is pointwise continuity, which holds as B is discrete.
acceptance: With the discrete topology on Hom(C, A), γ need not be continuous (HW23 E10).

nodes.title: The connecting map is cup product with the torsor class
nodes.statement: In the situation of splitting-torsor, for every m ≥ 0 and continuous m-cocycle c with values in C, s∘c is a continuous cochain with d(s∘c)(g_0, …, g_m) = γ(g_0)(g_0 c(g_1, …, g_m)); hence the connecting map H^m(Γ, C) → H^{m+1}(Γ, A) is ∂[c] = [γ ∪ c] for the evaluation pairing Hom_pt(C, A) × C → A.
hypotheses: As in splitting-torsor; cup products on continuous cochains with the jointly continuous evaluation pairing.
proofSteps: Direct computation on inhomogeneous cochains; no Ext interpretation is used.
acceptance: For finitely generated C the formula holds with discrete Hom and Tau Ceti's discrete cup product.

nodes.statement: If C is finitely generated as an abelian group, Hom_pt(C, A) is discrete, the splitting class lies in the discrete-module cohomology H^1(Γ, Hom(C, A)), and connecting-cup-formula holds with the discrete Hom and the discrete cup product; in particular for finite C, as in every application of Harpaz–Wittenberg's Lemma 5.5.

acceptance: This is the scope in which the printed Lemma 5.5 is correct.

sourceIssues.locator: §5, Lemma 5.5, p. 19 (author final version; corrected in PAPER-HARPAZ-WITTENBERG-23/E10)
sourceIssues.printed: Let Γ be a profinite group and 0 → A → B → C → 0 be a short exact sequence of discrete Γ-modules whose underlying sequence of abelian groups is split. ... Let [γ] ∈ H1(Γ, Hom(C, A)) be the class of this torsor.
sourceIssues.correction: Assume C finitely generated (for example finite, as in the only application), or give Hom(C, A) the pointwise topology Hom_pt(C, A), in which case the class lies in H^1(Γ, Hom_pt(C, A)) and the formula holds by a cochain computation.
sourceIssues.reason: Γ = ∏_ℕ C₂, A = ⊕𝔽₂a_i, C = ⊕𝔽₂c_i with trivial actions and B = A ⊕ C with g·c_i = c_i + g_i a_i: B is a discrete module and the sequence splits additively, but γ(g)(c_i) = g_i a_i has kernel {1}, not open, so γ is not continuous into the discrete module Hom(C, A).
